Notice that $B$ is the $3$rd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}.$

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ by the $3$rd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3},$ the result must be the $3$rd *column* of $A.$ Therefore,

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{6} \\ \sqrt{6} \\ -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 & -2\sqrt{6} \\ -1 & 7 & \sqrt{6} \\ 5 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot 0+(-2\sqrt{6})\cdot 1 \\ (-1)\cdot 0+7\cdot 0+\sqrt{6}\cdot 1 \\ 5\cdot 0+0\cdot 0+(-8)\cdot 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{6} \\ \sqrt{6} \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
